property_summary: A valid Deposit call that sends a nonzero amount should not revert when the contract is in normal state.
When calling Deposit with a positive ether amount, the call must not revert (i.e., succeeds) for a freshly funded tester account.
A Deposit call that sends amount v from this test contract should not revert when the test contract has at least v wei available.
If this test contract has at least amount wei and calls Deposit sending amount>0, the call must succeed (not revert).

Invariant: For any caller and any amounts, a successful Collect(x) call on the reference never decreases any account's stored balance below the stored balance prior to the call increased by any Deposits that occurred before Collect; the mutant that subtracts msg.value on Deposit can make some account's balances differ after Collect (specifically, Deposits by any address reduce balances, allowing Collect to produce different balances).

For any depositor A, after A deposits an amount d and then calls Collect(x) (with x ≤ previous balance and previous balance ≥ MinSum), the reference preserves that A's stored balance equals prior_balance - x; the mutant that subtracts msg.value on Deposit can make stored balances incorrect (Deposit reduces balance) and thus after Collect the stored balance differs for some inputs.

For any depositor and any amounts, if a depositor D first makes a Deposit of value v and then (possibly later) calls Collect(x) with x <= previous_balance and previous_balance >= MinSum, then the reference contract's stored balances[D] after Collect equals previous_balance - x; the mutant that subtracts msg.value during Deposit can make balances differ for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor and any amounts, if someone (any address) deposits value v and later Collect(_am) executes successfully, then the stored balance for that depositor after Collect equals its balance before Collect minus the collected amount; the mutant that subtracts msg.value on Deposit can make some depositor's balance differ after Collect for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor and any amounts, if a depositor D has balances[D] >= MinSum and then calls Collect(x) with x <= balances[D], the reference contract will successfully transfer x and leave balances[D] decreased by exactly x (i.e. new balance = old balance - x); the mutant that subtracts msg.value during Deposit can cause balances to be different after Collect for some fuzzed inputs.
